1944, June 8
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M. Cap.
St. Bonaventure Monastery 1740 Mt. Elliott Ave. Detroit, Mich. June 8th 1944
Rev. M. E. Joachim Casey Mt. Hope, Baltimore, Maryland.
My Dear Brother Maurice, Father Joachim: --
God bless you and yours -- including my poor self I hope. I received your welcome letter yesterday and, while there is a silent note therein of dis- satisfaction, that I can hardly be surprized at or blame you for, yet I am more than pleased and I thank God for what, in my opinion, must please Heaven better than any success you ever had -- or could have without it -- on missions, parishes or catechism teachings. Thank God for your tone of patient resignation, at once a great promoter and a fruit of Christian humility. God himself has provide in your present trying circumstances, a mill in His wisdom and in His mercy for your refinement in these virtues that pleas Him most. It seems to me a most hopeful indication if, notwithstanding your blunders as well as your successes for three and thirty years in the holy Priesthood -- in the brunt of the warfare, therefore -- and especially under your present trying circumstances, you can still sigh: "Non nobis Domine! non nobis ... ". Its God and His holy grace more than anything else that we ought thak. Blessed be His Holy Name!
About a year ago, on occasion of his 60th anniversary as a priest the renowned Pastor of Ironton, Ohio-outstanding lecturer and writer -- Father Cotter, told of his saintly and venerated sister then recently deceased, that when he had come into her presence after just hearing all kinds of laudations on occasion of his jubilee ten years before, she earnestly and honestly exclaimed: "0 James! How we ought to thank God that for these fifty years He has never per- mitted you to/any real scandal."
So dear Brother, Fr. Joachim: let us be grateful to God for everything -- the knocks we get as well as the consolations. ... and do not blame the Father Chaplain too severely if he seem unduly exacting, etc. Of all positions he has one that in my opinion must
